title: PDF Tools — Merge, Split and Compress PDF Files in Your Browser

content.intro: Combining multiple PDFs should not require expensive software. The PDF Tools page handles three jobs in one place — merging several files into one document, splitting a document apart, and compressing a file to reduce its size. Everything runs in your browser using PDF.js and the browser file APIs, so no PDF is uploaded to a server.

sections.heading: Why Local Processing Matters
sections.body: Most online PDF tools upload your file to a server — a privacy risk for contracts, invoices and anything else confidential. This page processes the file locally with PDF.js and the browser file APIs instead. Your document never leaves your computer, and because there is no upload step, the work also keeps working on a slow connection.

sections.heading: How to Merge PDFs
sections.body: Open the Merge PDFs tab, select one or more PDF files with the file picker, then run the operation. The selected files are concatenated into a single document in the order you picked them, and the result downloads as a new PDF. The same page also has a Split PDF tab for breaking one document into separate files, and a Compress PDF tab for reducing the size of a single file.

sections.heading: What the Tool Does and Does Not Do
sections.body: The page covers three operations: merging multiple files into one, splitting a single document, and compressing a single file. It is a focused utility rather than a full PDF editor — it does not reorder pages inside a document, does not open password-protected PDFs, and does not edit text, images or metadata. For those jobs, a dedicated desktop editor is the better tool.

sections.heading: Common Use Cases
sections.body: Combine monthly reports into a quarterly document. Consolidate invoices into one file for accounting. Split a long document into per-chapter files. Reduce the size of a scanned PDF before emailing it. Assemble a reading packet from separate articles.

content.conclusion: PDF merging shouldn't cost money or compromise privacy. Craftisle's Merger is free, fast, and secure — everything stays in your browser. Bookmark it for your next document assembly task.

keyTakeaways: The PDF Tools page merges, splits and compresses PDF files entirely in the browser.
No PDF is uploaded to a server — processing happens locally with PDF.js.
It is a focused utility, not a full editor: no page reordering, no password-protected files, no text editing.
Free, no registration and no watermarks on the output.
The same page handles all three jobs, so you do not need to switch tools.
